historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (14.6%) diverges >30% from EPS 5y (25.8%). EPS 5y starts at the COVID trough (FY2020 $12.24), and equity is shrunk by ~$7.6B of buybacks FY2021-25. The 3-year window (equity 8.3% vs EPS 9.1% vs revenue 11.4%) is the coherent one. Revenue CAGRs include acquisitions (Ahern Dec-2022, Yak 2024), so organic growth is lower.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (company FCF - SBC - est. equity-award withholding): FY2020 2,350 (2,440-90), FY2022 1,597 (1,764-167), FY2025 2,002 (2,181-179). Reported FCF: FY20 2,440, FY21 1,514, FY22 1,764, FY23 2,306, FY24 2,058, FY25 2,181 (Q4 earnings releases, 8-K ex99.1). The 5y FCF CAGR is negative because FY2020 was a capex-harvest year (gross rental capex cut to ~$1.0B), which is a cyclical artefact and not a trend. The owner 3y CAGR (7.8%) slightly exceeds reported (7.3%) because SBC fell as a share of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA margin has faded from the FY2022 peak of 48.3% to 47.8% (FY23), 46.7% (FY24), 45.5% (FY25) and 45.2% TTM ex-gain, on Specialty ancillary/re-rent mix. Sources: SEC XBRL companyfacts, URI Q4-2021/2023/2025 and Q2-2026 earnings releases.

scenario_narratives.base: URI delivers the raised FY2026 guide (revenue ~$17.65B, adjusted EBITDA ~$8.05B) and grows organically 5-6% thereafter, from rental penetration, Specialty cold-starts and cross-sell, and positive fleet productivity. Growth is funded by fleet capex that runs at ~18% of revenue plus ~1x the growth rate. The data-center build normalises around 2029 into one soft year (+2%, margin -1pp, capex cut to replacement), then growth resumes. Margins settle at 44.5%, below the 2022-24 peak because Specialty's ancillary/re-rent mix is structurally lower-margin. Permanent 100% bonus depreciation keeps cash taxes on (EBITDA - capex) rather than book EBIT. Tuck-in M&A is excluded on both sides.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI/data-center, fab, LNG and grid megaproject cycle proves a decade-long capex supercycle rather than a 2025-27 bulge. URI's national-account scale wins a disproportionate share of megaprojects. Specialty (power/HVAC, fluid, trench, mobile storage) compounds at 15-20%. Group revenue grows 8-10% for four years and margins recover to 46.5% as Specialty matures and the post-2025 cost programme lands. Capital discipline (walking away from H&E) keeps returns high, and fleet productivity gains trim capex intensity.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI capex is the marginal driver and it stalls in 2027. Megaproject backlogs slip, and the non-data-center nonresidential market, already flat to down in 2026, rolls into a cyclical downturn as 5%+ long rates bite on private construction. Revenue falls ~13% peak to trough over two years. Rates and time utilization drop together, used-equipment values fall (lower gains), and adjusted EBITDA margin troughs at 39.5%. URI does what it did in 2009 and 2020, slashing capex and harvesting cash, so FCF holds up in the trough but the rebuild costs it later. A larger Herc (post-H&E) and Sunbelt compete on price for national accounts, so mid-cycle margin settles 2pp lower at 42.5%, with tariffs inflating fleet replacement cost.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF for a cyclical, fleet-capital-intensive renter. The flows are adjusted EBITDA less SBC and equity-award withholding, less fleet capex net of the NBV of fleet sold (the gain on sale is already in EBITDA), less cash tax on the full-expensing base, less working capital on growth. Capex is tied to growth by a structural identity, so faster growth is not free. The model values URI on its cash generation after the reinvestment needed to grow. Its fleet capex absorbs roughly 55% of adjusted EBITDA in a growth year, which is why a DCF at a 10.5% WACC lands far below a market price that capitalises EBITDA at ~10x forward. The gap is the market paying for a sustained megaproject cycle (the bull case) at a discount rate well below this model's.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: at a 9% WACC (UST back near 4%) the base value rises materially; see the sensitivity grid. The 10y UST at 5.28% is the single largest valuation input.
Bonus depreciation: the tax path assumes OBBBA's permanent 100% expensing. A repeal reverts to book-basis cash taxes and cuts value.
Capex intensity: the 18% + 1.03 x g identity assumes current fleet productivity. Rate or time-utilization gains (+2.9% YTD) lower it; tariff-driven OEM inflation raises it.
Cycle timing: the base carries one soft year in Y4. An earlier or deeper downturn moves value toward the bear, though URI's cash harvest cushions the trough FCF.
Megaproject concentration: AI/data-center construction spending (+70% YoY in 2026) is the marginal driver. A pause hits Specialty power/HVAC and large-project General Rentals together.
Competitive structure: Herc's absorption of H&E creates a stronger #3. Pricing discipline in national accounts is the swing factor for mid-cycle margin.
Organic-only growth: tuck-in acquisitions are excluded from both the flows and the growth paths. Value-accretive M&A is upside not captured.

inputs.sbc_source: Stock compensation expense, net (the cash-flow add-back, which is the same figure as the adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line, so URI publishes no separate combined figure): FY2025 134 + H1-26 79 - H1-25 70 = TTM 143. Plus tax withholding for share-based compensation from the 10-Q equity statement: H1-26 48, plus an estimated ~5 for H2-25 because RSU vesting is concentrated in Q1, giving ~53. Total TTM 196 = 1.16% of TTM revenue. The two lines are summed because no combined figure is published.
inputs.share_count_basis: 62.24M basic shares on the 10-Q cover (as of 2026-07-20) plus ~0.15M dilutive RSUs (Q2-26 diluted weighted average 62.6M against 62.6M basic, and H1 RSU dilution 0.1M) = 62.4M fully diluted. Held FLAT because SBC plus withholding taxes are expensed in the flows. URI is a heavy repurchaser: about $2.0B TTM of program buybacks (FY2025 1,969 and H1-26 816 including withholding), a new $5B authorisation, and $1.5B guided for 2026. So the flat count is funded with cash, and the buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime; live, not a frozen quote; 5-day closes populated)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows at a USD rate. 10y UST 5.28% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-02). ERP 4.5%. Beta 1.35, an adjusted beta for a late-cycle, moderately levered equipment renter. That gives Ke = 11.4%. Pre-tax Kd ~6.3% (recent notes ~6%; marginal cost with the 10y at 5.3%), 4.8% after tax. Weights at market: E ~$67.4B, net debt $14.1B, so E/V ~83%. WACC = 0.83 x 11.4 + 0.17 x 4.8 = 10.3%, rounded to 10.5% because the cost of debt reprices higher as the 2021-vintage ~3.75% notes roll. The same WACC is used in every scenario: cyclical risk is charged in the flows (the base carries a soft year, the bear a recession), not with a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. URI reports under US GAAP ASC 842, so operating-lease cost (cash payments $371M FY2025) is already inside adjusted EBITDA. Operating-lease liabilities (~$1.16B non-current at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. No finance-lease adjustment: finance leases are immaterial and already inside total debt. lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. All subsidiaries are wholly owned.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, scenario-weighted. Routing: URI is a capital-intensive, cyclical US operating company (equipment rental). It is not a bank, REIT, holdco or LIC, so the SKILL.md routing table sends it to owner-FCF plus the cyclical adaptations (risk charged once; one lease treatment). This is the first valuation of the ticker, so there is no MEMORY entry and no prior model to match. 

FY0 BASIS: trailing twelve months to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 + H1-26 - H1-25), so the flows start where the latest balance sheet stops. Using FY2025 as FY0 with a June balance sheet would double-count the H1-26 FCF ($1.15B) that already sits in June net debt. TTM: revenue 16,832; adjusted EBITDA 7,662 (45.5%), or 7,613 (45.2%) excluding the $49M Q2-26 scaffolding-sale gain; reported FCF 2,132 (company definition: OCF less net equipment purchases, including restructuring payments). Y1 = Jul-26 to Jun-27, discounted a full year (house end-of-year convention; this is slightly conservative because Y1 ends ~9 months after the valuation date). 

CAPEX DEFINITION (key for a renter): the engine capex line = gross rental capex - NBV of rental fleet sold + net non-rental capex. The reason is that adjusted EBITDA already contains the GAIN on used-equipment sales (proceeds in revenue, NBV in cost of sales). So cash = EBITDA + NBV - gross capex, and subtracting capex net of full proceeds would count the gain twice. TTM engine capex = 4,748 gross rental - 763 NBV sold + 261 net non-rental = 4,246 (25.2% of revenue), consistent with FY2026 guidance (gross 4.85-5.25B, proceeds 1.35-1.55B, non-rental net 0.3-0.4B, which gives ~26%). Structural identity used for every year: capex% ~= rental depreciation (~16.4% of revenue) + growth x net-fleet/revenue (~1.03) + net non-rental (~1.6%), i.e. ~18% + 1.03 x g. This ties capex to growth in every scenario and lets the downturn harvest cash, as 2009 and 2020 did. 

TAX: the da_pct_path is TAX depreciation, not book D&A. OBBBA (Jul-2025) made 100% bonus depreciation permanent, so URI deducts gross fleet purchases immediately, and fleet sold has zero tax basis. Cash-taxable operating income is therefore EBITDA - SBC - (gross capex - NBV sold) = EBITDA - SBC - engine capex. That is why da_pct_path equals capex_pct_path exactly. Book D&A for reference: rental 2,767 + non-rental 446 = 3,213 TTM (19.1%). The cash tax rate ramps 15% -> 20% -> 24% (21% federal plus state and foreign). Actual TTM cash taxes were only $220M (FY25 602 + H1-26 158 - H1-25 540) because of the bonus-depreciation transition and the deferred tax build (+$405M FY25, +$220M H1-26). 

WORKING CAPITAL: negative capture (-8% of incremental revenue), since receivables (~16.6% of revenue) build with growth and release in a downturn. Payables swing with capex timing and net out over a year. 

INTEREST INCOME: 0. URI is net-debt, and cash at $112M is operating float. 

M&A: tuck-ins ($357M FY25, $400M H1-26) are NOT in FCF, so the growth paths are organic only. Acquired growth would need its acquisition spend charged. H&E: terminated; the $52M merger-termination benefit fell in H1-25, so it is outside the TTM base.

bear.rationale: AI-capex pullback in 2027 removes the megaproject driver just as non-data-center nonres (already flat) rolls over. Revenue falls 4% then 9% (2020 was -9%; 2009 was -24%). Used-equipment values fall with rates and margin troughs at 39.5% (fixed-cost deleverage plus lower used gains). URI harvests the fleet as in 2009/2020 (capex to 9-13% of revenue), and receivables release cash. Recovery then rebuilds the fleet at above-structural capex. Herc's enlarged scale pressures national-account pricing, so mid-cycle margin settles at 42.5%. Terminal 2.5%, 12x cap.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 8% = H2-26 at the raised FY26 guide midpoint ($17.65B, implying H2 +9.7% YoY) plus H1-27 at ~+6%. Then organic growth (rental penetration, Specialty cross-sell, ~40 cold-starts/yr, rate) of 5-6%, with one soft year (Y4, +2%) as the data-center build normalises and non-data-center nonres stays flat. That is an expected-value cycle, not a recession. 3.5% by Y10.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: TTM 45.2% ex scaffolding gain; FY26 guide 45.3-45.7%. Specialty mix (ancillary/re-rent) drags; G&R margin is improving. Dips ~1.5pp in the soft year (fixed-cost deleverage) and settles at 44.5%, below the 2022-24 peak of 46.7-48.3% and above the 2020 COVID trough.
base.capex_rationale: Capex % ~= 18% + 1.03 x growth (rental depreciation 16.4% + growth on a net fleet ~1.03x revenue + 1.6% net non-rental). Y1 25.8% matches FY26 guidance (~26%). The soft year cuts to 19.5% (replacement only). Terminal 21.5% supports the 3.5% Y10 growth; at 3% perpetual growth it would be ~21.1%, so the Gordon flow is slightly conservative.

bull.rationale: The data-center / reshoring / grid megaproject wave runs through the decade with no cyclical air-pocket. Specialty compounds at 15-20% and lifts group growth to high single digits. Margin recovers to 46.5% (G&R density, cost programme, Specialty mix matures). Capex intensity runs slightly below the structural line (fleet productivity +2-3%/yr). Terminal 3.5%, 16x cap.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): URI is a late-cycle, capital-goods-adjacent renter at record margins and record EBITDA. Its marginal growth driver is concentrated in AI/data-center capex. The non-data-center nonresidential market is already flat to down. 5%+ long rates weigh on private construction. Leverage is moderate (1.8x net), so the bear is a cyclical earnings and multiple event, not a solvency event, which is why it is not higher. Base 50%: the guide has been raised twice in 2026 and backlogs are strong, so the near-term path is well supported. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs the megaproject wave to persist for most of a decade AND margins to recover against Specialty mix drag, which are two independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
